To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CD8hi+ CD57+ T lymphocyte subset is enriched in antigen-specific cells and down-regulates their own cytolytical potential, and that the CD8+CD45RA+ subset, which includes naive and memory T cells, is the major source of the CD8+ CD57+ population.
CD8hiCD57+ T cells are enriched in HIV-specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) and that these cells down-modulate their cytotoxic activity.

the CD8hi+57+ cells are a population of activated cytotoxic T cells with a reduced ability to kill target cells and that this population can be expanded by in vitro activation with mitogens and HIV antigens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the CD57 antigen on CD8+ lymphocytes and the role of CD8hiCD57+ T cells during HIV infection.
the mechanisms of CD57+ T cell expansion during persistent viral infection and transplantation.
the study of CD8+ CD57+ cells and their role in the control of immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD57 marker is a marker of a subset of cytotoxic T cells that is activated and that is capable of producing the ICF, but not of proliferating in response to CD3 triggering.

CD8hiCD57+ cells are a subset of terminally differentiated cytolytic effector cells which are enriched in HIV-specific cells, down-modulate their cytolytic potential and participate in a negative control in persistent viral infections and transplantations.
the CD8hi+57+ cells are a terminal differentiated state of activated cytotoxic T cells that are enriched for HIV-specific T cells and can down-modulate their cytolytic potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD8hiCD57+ lymphocytes are enriched for antigen-specific T cells that are capable of inhibiting cytolytic activity, thus playing a role in the control of cytotoxic T cell responses in HIV infection.

CD8hiCD57+ T cells are activated cytotoxic T cells which down-modulate their cytotoxic activity and are enriched in antigen specific cells, and that these cells are expanded during HIV infection and after bone marrow transplantation, probably as a consequence of the persistent stimulation by the virus or the graft.
the CD8hi+ CD57+ T lymphocyte population is an activated effector cell population which has a high cytotoxic capacity and a low proliferative potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CD8+CD28-CD57+ T cells are a population of memory CD8+ T cells which are enriched in HIV-specific cells.
CD8hiCD57+ T cells are enriched in antigen specific T cells and down modulate their own cytotoxic potential.
CD8hi CD57+ T cells have an activated memory T cell phenotype.
